title: What a genome-editing readout can justify
subtitle: A claim-linked reading graph of product-dependent observability and sequence correspondence
articleTitle: Product dependent observability and sequence correspondence in genome editing readouts
author: Facundo Firmenich

scope.description: Article-specific authored argument map with progressive explanation and frozen source bindings.
scope.epistemicStatus: Proposed communication artifact. It introduces no new observations, experiments, independent validation or mathematical priority claim.
scope.privacy: Public diagram and computational companion authorized for repository update on 29 October 2026. The complete manuscript, formal supplement and source snapshots remain private pending the author-defined preprint deposition.
scope.readability: Student, technical and audit levels refer to the same statements and fact IDs; simplified prose must not strengthen claims.
scope.mapSemantics: Typed navigation and declared support dependencies. A line is not a causal effect, posterior probability or automatic proof.
notClaims: First or universally novel graph format
scope.coverageContract: Twelve reading stations connect the study question, operations, source-bound quantities, conditional derivations, adverse cases and limits. This public diagram is a scientific summary; the private full-text subsection routing map is not distributed.
scope.baselineVersion: Two withheld full-text byte identities refer to the pre-MP04 source baseline. They are identity records only, not distributed files or current manuscript hashes. Eleven numerical/model sources refer to exact already-public repository files.

stations.title: What does an editing percentage actually establish?
stations.question: Can the intended product alter whether it is observed, and can equal labels conceal different sequences?
stations.takeaway: An editing readout needs an observation contract before it can support a product claim.

levels.student: A DNA read is a finite recorded sequence. A rule chooses which recorded segment to extract and which event to count. If that rule misses the intended product, a percentage may change even when the input reads do not. This article asks what the recorded data can justify under explicit rules.
levels.technical: The biological programme concerns a pertinent product on an expressible allele, compatible RNA and protein, function and bounded injury. P1 addresses one necessary observation dependency: finite-read censoring, observed-string correspondence and target-relative representation. It does not complete the product-to-function conjunction.
levels.audit: The source interventions and functional experiments belong to Sousa et al. The computational audit is retrospective within one CFTR genealogy, with an external convenience collection. Graph position and colour describe argument roles; they do not encode causal strength, posterior probability or scientific priority.

rivals.explanation: Every editing percentage can be compared as the same quantity.
rivals.discriminator: Declare the event, universe, extraction and reference; compare like contracts before numerical ranking.

stations.revisionCondition: A scope-complete product, transcript, protein, functional and injury assessment would extend the biological claim; the current read-level result cannot substitute for it.
stations.consequence: Keep the larger genetic-improvement programme visible while locating exactly which observational dependency this paper establishes.
stations.printSummary: Bind every percentage to an observation contract.

stations.title: Fix the unit, event and denominator
stations.question: What exactly is being counted, in which recorded universe?
stations.takeaway: Local peptide equivalence, exact programmed DNA and software MODIFIED are different events.

levels.student: The main event is local DNA whose computer translation matches the stated peptide. That differs from exact programmed DNA and from a software label counting changes under its chosen region and rules. Unknown reads stay in the original denominator instead of disappearing from the percentage.
levels.technical: Native local translation is the in-silico predicate GTIKENIIFGVSYD on the extracted local coding DNA. Exact CTT-plus-full-SE2 coding is a separate predicate. Built-in CRISPResso 2 MODIFIED/aligned uses its own software event and aligned-record denominator after the shared original-read Q30 prefilter.
levels.audit: Stream identity, orientation, quality policy, extraction boundaries, event predicate, transform and information timing belong to the contract. The fifteen deduplicated streams and nine-stream primary subset have different scopes. Read records are not donors, cells, unique molecules or biological replicates.

rivals.explanation: A change in the native software percentage must imply a change in native local correction.
rivals.discriminator: Hold the local DNA event and original raw denominator fixed, and retain MODIFIED/aligned separately.

stations.revisionCondition: Correct a comparison if either arm silently changes its event, sequence boundary, quality mask or denominator.
stations.consequence: Attach the event and denominator to every displayed percentage and contrast.

details.title: Separate source-software and common-event comparisons
details.text: Table 4A retains built-in MODIFIED/aligned. Table 4B holds the native local DNA translation event and original raw N fixed across the two observed-base projections and common-string witness. Per-arm event hulls, treated-minus-control contrasts and native software percentages answer different questions and must not share an unqualified percent axis.

details.title: This configured audit complements established tool capabilities
details.text: ampliCan normalizes individual insertion, deletion and mismatch events while preserving other putative events on a read. CRISPResso 2 also offers dedicated prime-editing, multiple-amplicon and ambiguity settings. This article audits local-product interchangeability under its declared configuration and adapter; it does not benchmark every setting or establish that the proposed observer is more accurate.

stations.printSummary: Local DNA, exact coding and software modification differ.

stations.title: A three-base displacement can hide a required anchor
stations.question: Can the product move a required observation feature beyond a finite read?
stations.takeaway: The documented anchor no longer fits after displacement; the same-input contrast depends on the observation rule.

levels.student: Imagine reading a sentence through a fixed-length window while requiring a word at its end. Adding three letters earlier can push that final word out of view. Here the documented shifted anchor ends at position 225 in a 224-base read. A missing required anchor leaves the record unknown; it does not prove absence of the intended DNA event.
levels.technical: Complete containment of the shifted anchor [a+d, a+d+m) in [0, L) requires 0≤a+d and a+d+m≤L. In the documented geometry a=210, m=12, L=224, d=3, the shifted interval[213, 225) fails. The shifted inner interval[206, 218) fits. Under common Q30, edge/inner/target native PE-minus-mock lower endpoints are −10.09177,+4.38081,+13.23196 pp in CFB-26-16.
levels.audit: The edge interval includes zero; a negative lower endpoint alone is not evidence of a negative contrast. Interrupted literal prefixes occur in 3071/3227 conditioned target-event records unresolved by the edge rule. That subset diagnostic does not estimate the causal fraction of the complete contrast or the capture rate of material never sequenced. The small inner-versus-edge ranking is not universally stable.

rivals.explanation: The discrepancy is entirely a changed quality gate.
rivals.discriminator: Compare the operators using the same original whole-read mask.

rivals.explanation: Every loss of an edge label is caused by the three-base displacement.
rivals.discriminator: Inspect complete anchors, prefix termination and other unresolved conditions record by record.

stations.revisionCondition: The read-end diagnosis weakens if the required complete anchor is present inside the affected records, or another declared failure condition explains the interrupted prefixes.
stations.consequence: Treat product-dependent observability as a concrete local mechanism; do not turn one operator contrast into a universal accuracy ranking.

details.title: A shorter record can remove ambiguity as well as evidence
details.text: The deterministic eight-base truncation holds the original whole-read mask fixed. A second candidate motif can disappear, making a nominal target label look newly resolved. The post hoc original-ambiguity veto restores U for such calls. Its target lower endpoint returns to 13.23196 pp, but the vetoed upper endpoint 22.82411 differs from the untrimmed 22.81439 pp. This is a censoring test on existing records, not a new short-read sequencing experiment.

stations.printTitle: The product can hide its anchor
stations.printSummary: Same reads; native PE−mock contrast under common Q30.

stations.title: Unknown records define a finite compatible set
stations.question: What can be concluded without assigning unobserved labels?
stations.takeaway: Retaining unknown mass yields sharp conditional extrema without assigning unobserved outcomes.

levels.student: If the accepted event and non-event labels are correct, the real treated example has 3563 events, 15846 non-events and 1164 unknowns, out of 20573 records. At least the accepted events count; at most those events plus every unknown count. Nothing here makes the middle of the interval most likely.
levels.technical: With E+NE+U=N, accepted-label correctness and unrestricted completion give the attainable fractions{(E+k)/N:k integer, 0≤k≤U}. Their hull is[E/N,(E+U)/N]. For treated minus control, the minimum assigns treated unknowns to non-event and control unknowns to event; the maximum reverses those assignments. Exact rational arithmetic precedes rounded display.
levels.audit: These are conditional finite-record identification hulls, not sampling confidence intervals, posterior credible intervals or population treatment effects. Accepted-label error or justified coupling between unknowns changes the model. Compatible refinement narrows the hull only when the same universe, event and resolved labels are preserved without conflict.

rivals.explanation: Unknown reads can be dropped or treated as event-free without changing the conclusion type.
rivals.discriminator: Recalculate the event fraction within the original N and retain both attainable extremes.

stations.revisionCondition: Recalculate if the partition fails, accepted labels are shown wrong, or the admissible completion class is independently constrained.
stations.consequence: Display exact extrema and the assumptions that make them sharp; do not visually imitate a confidence interval.

details.title: Compatible refinement is a conditional monotonicity result
details.text: Proposition 3 narrows a hull only when operator B preserves every accepted label of A on the same event and raw universe while resolving some U. An E-versus-NE conflict makes the joint accepted constraints inconsistent under the model that both are correct; majority voting does not repair the premise. Segment-contract changes do not satisfy compatible refinement merely because the high-level event names agree.

stations.printSummary: Finite bounds require stated label and completion premises.

stations.title: An agreeing label need not identify an agreeing string
stations.question: Do two outputs labelled with the same event refer to the same observed segment?
stations.takeaway: Reference-sensitive labels and actual equal-label/unequal-string records refute simple interchangeability.

levels.student: A label compresses information. Two different written sequences can receive the same yes/no label, just as different words can both be called nouns. In these data, some coding strings differ even when their native-event labels agree. Agreement of labels therefore cannot stand in for comparison of the strings.
levels.technical: Replacing the frozen mutant core with the programmed core changed 137 resolved native labels under the declared observed-base projection adapter. Among 170808 jointly resolved records, 83 coding strings differed;18 of those disagreements retained the same event label. No input read had to change for the representation to change.
levels.audit: The second reference stress test was post hoc. It diagnoses the declared generic amplicon configuration and adapter, not every CRISPResso 2 setting. Dedicated prime-editing, multi-amplicon and ambiguity configurations were not benchmarked. Repeated identical strings also cannot establish a unique physical molecule or positional copy.

rivals.explanation: Equal event labels guarantee the same coding sequence.
rivals.discriminator: Compare the actual oriented observed coding strings for each common record.

rivals.explanation: A changed label proves one reference is biologically correct.
rivals.discriminator: Supply an authenticated independent truth channel.

stations.revisionCondition: Revise the correspondence claim if orientation, boundary or matching errors remove the inspected unequal-string cases.
stations.consequence: Require the correspondence level needed by the claim before joining outputs across observers.

details.title: A recorded example does not identify its molecular origin
details.text: The two inspectable SRR29623270 examples have read lengths 300 and 299. Target motifs and the programmed reference extract 42 coding bases, while the mutant reference projects 87 and 89. These are actual observed sequence disagreements with repeated target-related content. The paper leaves biological duplication, amplification and sequencing origins unresolved.

stations.printSummary: Compare observed coding strings before joining outputs.
stations.printEvidence:
170,808 joint; 83 unequal strings;
18 retain equal native-event labels.

stations.title: Accept a common coding string before classifying it
stations.question: What is the conservative shared observed-sequence domain?
stations.takeaway: The witness accepts only identical observed strings from three declared extractions.

levels.student: The witness asks three procedures for the local coding string: target motifs and the two baseline projections. A record is accepted only when all three return the same oriented string. Everything else stays unknown. Requiring more agreement reduces what is accepted and can widen the honest compatible range.
levels.technical: The conjunction is: target extraction resolved AND mutant projection resolved AND programmed projection resolved AND exact observed-string equality. The event predicate is then applied to that common string. The witness retains 170725 records and 6281 unknowns inside N=177006. It is a subset of the target-resolved domain, not a vote over event labels.
levels.audit: Under a shared event and accepted-label contract, the witness hull contains the target hull: stronger correspondence requirements can cost resolution. The original witness uses the two frozen baselines; it was not redefined after seeing fourteen parameter profiles. String equality establishes record-level observed sequence correspondence, not full-allele or molecular identity.

rivals.explanation: More agreement must always produce a narrower interval.
rivals.discriminator: Count labels deliberately returned to unknown by the stricter shared-string requirement.

rivals.explanation: Three agreeing extractions provide independent biological truth.
rivals.discriminator: Distinguish shared-read computations from independent molecular evidence.

stations.revisionCondition: Correct the witness if any accepted record fails one extraction or the exact oriented-string equality contract.
stations.consequence: Use the conservative witness where correspondence is essential; retain its loss of resolution as an explicit cost.

details.title: Keep the reasons for unknown status disjoint
details.text: The 6281 witness unknowns partition into 1996 quality failures, 4202 missing-correspondence cases and 83 coding disagreements. Quality failure takes priority in this partition. These are observation-status categories, not new biological species and not the overlapping E/NE conflict scopes counted in the sensitivity grid.

stations.printEvidence:
170,725 / 177,006 retained; 6,281 U.
Target + two baseline projections.

stations.title: State the positive result at its actual strength
stations.question: Which contrast remains positive under every allowed unknown completion?
stations.takeaway: All three native witness PE-minus-mock lower endpoints are positive under the stated premises.

levels.student: If the accepted event and non-event labels are correct, the shared-string native local event contrast is positive in all three nominal preparations even under the least favourable allowed unknown completion. This is a result about these sequenced records and this event. It is not a measurement of restored protein function.
levels.technical: The native witness PE-minus-mock hulls are[13.23196, 22.96507],[27.13342, 34.30984] and[23.15888, 30.03680] pp. The exact lower endpoint in the worked first preparation is 3563/20573−702/17177=6679915/50483203. Positivity follows from the finite completion extremes and the accepted-label premise.
levels.audit: Minimum individual-label withdrawals that remove strict positivity are 2273, 5206 and 3398 for these three native PE-minus-mock contrasts. This is a hypothetical sensitivity on actual capacities, not an estimated error rate. Withdrawing whole identical-coding families is a different objective: one family suffices under the declared grouping, affecting 3541, 5605 and 3706 assignments.

rivals.explanation: A positive finite-record lower endpoint identifies a population or clinical effect.
rivals.discriminator: Authenticate biological units and obtain an appropriate biological design and functional outcome.

rivals.explanation: Withdrawal counts estimate how many errors actually occurred.
rivals.discriminator: Separate deterministic sensitivity from empirical error calibration.

stations.revisionCondition: The positive certificate changes if source reconstruction fails, accepted labels are withdrawn under a declared alternative contract, or independent truth reveals accepted-label error.
stations.consequence: Retain this conditional local victory without promoting it to biological accuracy, independence or function.

details.title: The withdrawal optimum is a finite sensitivity certificate
details.text: For a positive lower contrast, withdrawing one treated E toU reduces it by 1/N_t; withdrawing one control NE reduces it by 1/N_c. The other two accepted-label classes do not reduce this endpoint. Choosing the largest available contributions first is exchange-optimal under the actual capacities. The source verifies afterK≤0 and afterK−1>0. This deterministic minimum is separate from whole-identical-coding-family withdrawal and supplies no measured error probability.

stations.printSummary: Native PE−mock positivity requires the accepted-label premise.

stations.title: Stable contrast signs can coexist with changing record labels
stations.question: Does a positive aggregate sign imply invariant assignments?
stations.takeaway: Finite-grid positivity and record-level stability are different properties.

levels.student: Changing an alignment setting can alter individual classifications while a treatment-versus-control bound stays positive. Looking only at the final sign hides those changes. The audit therefore checks both the contrast and which record identifiers change labels.
levels.technical: The article reports 144 executed jobs:126 in fourteen reference-by-OAT profiles and 18 separate stock jobs. Native projected PE-minus-mock minimum lower endpoints over the OAT family are 16.01852, 29.05794 and 25.16093 pp. The full family contains 163 native and 161 exact-event conflicting identifiers, including 137 and 135 conflicts already present between the baselines.
levels.audit: The expanded family adds 26 conflicting identifiers per event; overlapping family counts are not additive. A stock profile changes several options jointly, so it cannot isolate window dependence. Stock projected-event counts matched the baselines even when MODIFIED/aligned changed. These are known-data retrospective stress tests, not prospective transport or truth calibration.

rivals.explanation: A stable positive sign proves the underlying classifications are robust.
rivals.discriminator: Inspect distinct-record E/NE conflicts within each specified profile family.

rivals.explanation: The stock result isolates one quantification-window effect.
rivals.discriminator: Recognize its jointly changed effective settings; isolate one change in a separate design.

stations.revisionCondition: A pinned rerun that changes the exact minima, assignments or configuration attribution requires correcting the finite-grid claim.
stations.consequence: Report aggregate extrema and record-level conflicts separately, with the precise tested family and timing.
stations.printSummary: Contrast stability does not imply record-label stability.
stations.printEvidence:
144 jobs / 14 OAT profiles;
163 native conflicts; stock separate.

stations.title: Ask what a representation preserves for a declared target
stations.question: When is a compressed representation sufficient for one observed target?
stations.takeaway: Observed-catalog factorization is target-relative and requires constancy within representation fibers.

levels.student: A summary is adequate only for a stated question. Group catalog entries that have the same summary. If two members of one group have different target answers, the summary cannot recover that target on these entries. Another target may still be preserved perfectly by the same summary.
levels.technical: For a finite resolved catalog C, representation r and target e, a function e_R with e=e_R∘r on C exists exactly when e is constant on every observed fiber of r. One actual equal-r/unequal-e pair refutes that finite factorization. The criterion is elementary and classical; no mathematical priority is claimed.
levels.audit: Joint target logic also matters. In the CFTR common-string domain, exact programmed coding implies native local translation, giving resolved signature counts 12852, 128 and 157745. For native-but-not-exact, the sharp hull is[128/177006, 6409/177006]. Independently subtracting marginal hulls loses that logical coupling and yields a looser outer range.

rivals.explanation: One universally best compressed representation preserves every scientific target.
rivals.discriminator: Fix the target and inspect actual within-fiber distinctions rather than rank summaries globally.

rivals.explanation: Subtracting marginal intervals always gives the sharp joint-event interval.
rivals.discriminator: Retain exact⇒native coupling on the shared resolved domain.

stations.revisionCondition: Revise the certificate if a real positive-weight equal-representation/unequal-target pair is found, or if the target or resolved domain changes.
stations.consequence: Choose representations for the declared question and observed support; do not certify unseen future dynamics.

details.title: Joint targets retain logic that marginal subtraction loses
details.text: Exact programmed coding implies the native local translation target under this contract. The native-but-not-exact resolved count is 128. Retaining that coupling gives the sharp hull[128/177006, 6409/177006]. Independently subtracting marginal hulls gives the looser outer hull[−6153/177006, 6409/177006]. Its negative lower endpoint is algebraic slack from the relaxed coupling, not a negative event count.

stations.printSummary: Check fibers and joint logic on resolved records.

stations.title: Keep the ambiguous and uninformative cases
stations.question: Can a correct finite certificate fail to demonstrate discrimination or complete-domain identity?
stations.takeaway: Ambiguous targets and constant target support constrain what a successful certificate means.

levels.student: A test can pass because every example has the same answer. That does not show an ability to tell different answers apart. A label can also leave the target unresolved. The paper keeps both situations visible instead of silently replacing ambiguity or calling every pass a useful success.
levels.technical: The external collection contains 10809 real rows from NHEJ, P23H/WT and EMX1. Source status plus reference does not preserve the full observed string in any catalog. In P23H/WT, 572 reference-ambiguous assignments remain unresolved for complete-template identity. In EMX1, complete-template equality is always false and full-alignment gap presence always true.
levels.audit: EMX1 is an interpretive constant-target control here, not a newly conducted biological negative-control experiment. Terminal gaps can satisfy the fixed alignment-text target outside the source quantification mask. Ninety overlapping deterministic checks do not supply ninety independent biological trials. The support-size diagnostic was added post hoc without rewriting the primary decisions.

rivals.explanation: Removing an AMBIGUOUS_ prefix authenticates one template origin.
rivals.discriminator: Inspect source reference-assignment semantics and tied references.

rivals.explanation: A factorization pass demonstrates discrimination even for a constant target.
rivals.discriminator: Report the number of observed target values and the resolved support.

stations.revisionCondition: A verified unique template mapping refines the P23H/WT domain; a prespecified evaluation with nonconstant target values is needed to test discrimination.
stations.consequence: Treat adverse, ambiguous and constant-support cases as essential boundaries of the result.

details.title: Whole-string differences do not imply source misclassification
details.text: In NHEJ, source lines 2 and 58 are both UNMODIFIED, while line 58 deletes reference position 9 outside the reported mask 15–117. Selected P23H/WT unequal strings delete position 165 outside quantification positions 89 and 90. Thus a legitimate local quantification label can coexist with a full-string difference. These coordinate diagnostics were post hoc and do not establish a molecular repair mechanism.

details.title: Aligned-catalog accounting does not reconstruct missing raw processing
details.text: NHEJ leaves 656 paired input units outside its aligned catalog; the single-end P23H/WT and EMX1 catalogs leave 374 and 30 raw records outside their tables. A multiset match is narrower than identifier-level preprocessing and alignment replay. The EMX1 documentation window parameter 10 also differs from the frozen report parameter 20; both declarations are retained without executing the alternate configuration or inventing an accuracy comparison.

stations.printSummary: Template ambiguity and constant targets limit the certificate.
stations.printEvidence:
P23H/WT: 572 U assignment weight
EMX1: two constant targets

stations.title: Reproduce computations and identify their shared sources
stations.question: What do independent implementations and clean replay actually verify?
stations.takeaway: Source identity and computational reproduction support consistency within the declared evidence scope.

levels.student: Another piece of code can repeat a calculation and catch implementation mistakes. Repeating it on the same reads does not create another group of people, cells or independent molecules. This paper keeps those two kinds of evidence separate.
levels.technical: The witness reconstruction uses the 177006 original primary records; a separate portable projection checker verifies 354012 per-reference labels and allele-abundance conservation using frozen alignments. Source hashes, exact fractions, commands, input identities and clean-directory reconstruction make these claims inspectable. Fresh engine execution is reported separately from frozen-alignment replay.
levels.audit: The observer family, truncation veto and second reference stress test are retrospective. External report summaries were visible before the protocol was privately frozen and row parsing began. No public biological preregistration, blinding, outside human reproduction, independent cohort or comparative molecular-accuracy assessment is asserted.

rivals.explanation: Two implementations on the same source records supply independent biological replication.
rivals.discriminator: Track the source genealogy and analyst/experimental independence explicitly.

rivals.explanation: A privately frozen known-data analysis is a prospective biological preregistration.
rivals.discriminator: Record what was known at freeze time and which operations occurred afterwards.

stations.revisionCondition: A source identity mismatch, failed exact reconstruction or identified implementation error requires correction; an authenticated external analyst can add a different level of reproduction evidence.
stations.consequence: Make the computational evidence auditable while naming exactly which kinds of independence remain absent.

details.title: An independently written checker can share the same evidence
details.text: The separate grouping implementation checks 90 certificates, 100 returned row-pair witnesses and three joint partitions. Returned pairs may reuse source rows. Clean-directory replay checks 27 inputs and regenerates six scientific files byte identically. The installed 0.2.0 wheel and actual-data contract tests verify specified software behaviours; they do not constitute another cohort, an outside human replication or a replay of the upstream source alignments.

stations.printSummary: Shared sources define what computation can verify.
stations.printEvidence:
177,006 raw / 354,012 per-ref labels
Shared-source alignment replay

stations.title: Carry the result forward without crossing its boundary
stations.question: What can change in reporting now, and what new evidence is required for stronger claims?
stations.takeaway: The practical proposal is a claim-specific reporting contract with explicit unresolved frontiers.

levels.student: A useful report should tell a reader what was counted, what stayed unknown, which sequence corresponded across methods and what would overturn the conclusion. That helps prevent a local DNA observation from silently becoming a claim about a functional protein or an improved cell.
levels.technical: The proposed contract binds raw universe, event, correspondence level, quality, transforms, E/NE/U, exact extrema, source identity and timing. It was exercised on 36 evidence cards and 24 compatible contrasts. The PaperGraph adds a navigable argument layer whose edges declare support, definition, limitation or required conjunction; it is not an independent theorem prover.
levels.audit: Independent truth is required for comparative molecular accuracy; authenticated specimen and aliquot links for product-to-function claims; prespecified new genealogies for transport; measured user outcomes for clarity or analyst-benefit claims. These remain separate frontiers. The PaperGraph itself needs usability evaluation before claims of better comprehension, faster review or fewer analytical errors.

rivals.explanation: A richer visual graph proves biological accuracy or improved reader performance.
rivals.discriminator: Evaluate molecular truth and user outcomes using appropriate independent evidence.

stations.revisionCondition: Narrow or correct any graph statement whose contract, source anchor, derivation or stated scope fails; stronger scientific or usability claims require their own evidence.
stations.consequence: Introduce the PaperGraph as an author-proposed, versioned article companion and a compact figure in the main text, keeping manuscript and complete companion private until the author deposits the preprint.

details.title: Keep the missing sample-to-function link visible
details.text: The primary preparation assignments do not supply an authenticated mapping to individual functional-assay columns. A local observed-DNA category cannot complete full allele, RNA, protein, function and injury links. A standard workflow that avoids this discrepancy would constrain practical generality and incremental utility; it would not by itself refute a different fixed observation contract.

details.title: Related author work is context rather than biological validation
details.text: The related tomography and projection preprints locate a wider methodological programme. The CRISPR claims here remain supported by the read-level analyses in this article. No physical equivalence, mathematical priority or biological validation follows from that bibliographic relationship.

details.title: Reporting software is not a demonstrated algorithmic advantage
details.text: Grouped factorization implements a classical condition. The article does not demonstrate an advantage over a simple grouping implementation. A finite scope checker verifies declared fields and rejections, while independent usability, analyst-error prevention, review-time savings and adoption require measured outcomes of their own.

stations.printSummary: State sources, conditions and what would revise the claim.
stations.printEvidence:
36 cards / 24 compatible contrasts.
Case-tested reporting proposal.
